content:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency crossing SLO on dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-pool-7' for serving route /generate (customers: AcmeCorp) — current p99 1.9s vs SLO 1.2s. Queue depth rising. Paging on-call (priya).

alex: saw the alert, joining. any degradation to streaming or just batch gen?

priya: both. streaming stalls reported by telemetry (stream chunk gaps), and overall p95->p99 gap widened. Queue depth on pool 7 is 420 requests, target drain threshold 50.

jane-sre: copying runbook section: "If dedicated pool queue > 300 and p99 > 1.5s, evaluate priming backlog, scale, and failover." Next steps: 1) assess autoscaler lag 2) consider manual scale 3) enable fallback routing for critical customers.

miguel: autoscaler logs show scale-up triggers at 1728209950 but new workers not registered until ~1728210100 — ~110s cold join. Looks like the pool priming (GPU init) is taking longer than expected under burst.

tim-eng: confirm. kernel init + model weight load is the slow path. We have a known roll with late OOM retries in the image that can add 30-60s. Was there a recent deployment to that fleet? ops-bot: deploys: no recent deploys in last 6h for pool-7.

priya: immediate mitigation suggestions? I can manual-scale but want to avoid overshooting committed capacity.

alex: prioritize customer impact. customer-success, do AcmeCorp seeing errors or just higher latency?

customer-success: AcmeOps says 'timeout spikes ~2m ago, some streaming sessions stalled (~10% sessions). No errors yet but UX impacted.' They asked if there's an ETA.

jane-sre: mitigation plan: A) spin up 4 warm (pre-primed) nodes from spare pool (manual) B) enable fallback-route for AcmeCorp to a compatible variant with lower memory (quantized v1) C) temporary queue throttle for non-critical routes to prioritize customer traffic.

miguel: commands to run (use with caution):
```
# manual scale (adds 4 primed nodes)
infractl pool resize --pool eu-west-2-pool-7 --add 4 --type primed
# enable fallback policy for customer
rtrctl set-route-policy --route /generate --customer AcmeCorp --fallback-model rdx-quant-v1
```

priya: executing manual scale now. tagging alex and jane for tracking. I'll also open a high-priority ticket with infra to investigate image slow-init.

alex: I'll enable fallback routing for AcmeCorp, set to permissive so we don't break outputs. lia, can you adjust queue weights to deprioritize low-pri routes?

lia: on it — lowering weight for /batch-reencode and /metrics-embed by 80% for 10m.

ops-bot: ATTEMPT: pool resize request queued. Estimated priming 60s per node, but primed cache may reduce time.

miguel: seeing new worker registration at 1728210115 (one-by-one). p99 dropped to 1.4s at 1728210160 — good trend. queue depth 190.

customer-success: AcmeOps reports streaming gaps reduced but still seeing some p99 spikes. They're okay with fallback if it stabilizes.

priya: enabling fallback now.

ops-bot: route-policy applied for AcmeCorp -> rdx-quant-v1. Traffic diversion at 1728210188.

alex: after diversion p99 is 1.0s and streaming stalls resolved at 1728210205. Queue depth 85. Good.

jane-sre: mitigation successful. Next: post-incident follow-ups: 1) investigate slow priming path and image OOM retries, 2) add predictive priming/alarm when burst expected, 3) run a canary of primed node flow to verify init time, 4) update runbook to include fallback routing quicker in step 1.

tim-eng: I'll triage image retries and submit a patch to reduce init latency. miguel can you capture core logs from slow nodes for offline analysis?

miguel: logs collected and uploaded to /mnt/incident-logs/1728210000-priming-slow.tar.gz. ticket INFRA-4219 created.

priya: calling incident 'capacity-threshold-throttle-handoff' for postmortem. Rough customer impact: AcmeCorp ~10% sessions degraded for ~6 minutes, no data loss. Flagging for SE outreach.

customer-success: I'll coordinate outreach and summary to AcmeOps.

jane-sre: closing on-call now — handoff notes in the ticket. If p99 creeps again we'll page SRE primary. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

alex: adding action items to the incident board. Good job team.

incident-bot: INCIDENT AUTO-CLOSE: no p99 regressions for 15m. Marking as resolved pending postmortem updates.
